content: Properly dispose of this medication when it is expired or no longer needed. Do not flush it down the toilet or pour it into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Follow local guidelines for medication disposal. This information was last updated in September 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your individual health needs. This medication, commonly known by the brand name Vantin, is used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It belongs to a class of drugs called cephalosporin antibiotics. It is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. If you are using the suspension form of this medication, it can be taken with or without food. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Medications that reduce or block stomach acid, such as proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), H2 blockers, or antacids, may decrease the absorption of cefpodoxime, potentially reducing its effectiveness. Consult your doctor or pharmacist on how to safely use these medications with cefpodoxime. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may allow the bacteria to continue growing, potentially leading to a relapse of the infection. Common side effects of this medication include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, or headache. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but can occur. Symptoms of a severe allergic reaction may include rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking cefpodoxime proxetil, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillins, or to other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cephalexin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may interfere with live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine), potentially reducing their effectiveness. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., Coombs' test, certain urine glucose tests), potentially causing false test results. Inform laboratory personnel and your doctors that you are using this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. Store the suspension in the refrigerator and do not freeze it. Discard any unused suspension after 14 days.
